messages.subject: Is it possible to obtain a Part 5 report with only 1 sleep period.
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to obtain a Part 5 report with only 1 sleep period.
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm hoping someone here might be able to help;

I'm working with some data where we have only 1 night's sleep for a (large) subset of individuals in our study. Part 2 and 4 report without any issue for these individuals but they do not appear in part 5. For each of these individuals we have at least 24hrs worth of recording but this only includes 1 night (2 days, 1 night).

Is there a way to obtain a part 5 report for these individuals? I've tried adjusting midnight (dayborder =) to give a complete 24hrs for timewindow = MM to no avail.

The script I'm using is:

g.shell.GGIR(#-------------------------------
             # General parameters
             #-------------------------------
             mode=mode,
             datadir=datadir,
             outputdir=outputdir,
             studyname=studyname,
             f0=f0,
             f1=f1,
             overwrite = TRUE,
             do.imp=TRUE,
             idloc=2,
             print.filename=FALSE,
             storefolderstructure = FALSE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),
             do.cal=TRUE,
             do.enmo = TRUE,
             do.anglez=TRUE,
             chunksize=1,
             printsummary=TRUE,
             do.parallel=TRUE,
             daylimit=FALSE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 1,
             ndayswindow=7,
             hrs.del.start = 0.05,
             hrs.del.end = 0.05,
             maxdur = 4,
             # includedaycrit = 4,
             # includenightcrit = 4,
             L5M5window = c(0,24),
             M5L5res = 10,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
             qwindow=c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
             mvpathreshold =c(100,120),
             # #-------------------------------
             # # Part 3 parameters:
             # #-------------------------------
             timethreshold= c(10),
             anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = FALSE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             loglocation= c(),
             excludefirstlast = FALSE,
             # includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(),
             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             threshold.lig = c(50),
             threshold.mod = c(100),
             threshold.vig = c(400),
             boutcriter = 0.8,
             boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,
             boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
             boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(10,30),
             boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1,10),
             timewindow = c("WW","MM"),
             excludefirstlast.part5 = FALSE,
             #dayborder = 10,
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             do.report=c(2,4,5))

Thanks in advance for any help you can provide,

Luke

messages.subject: Re: Sleep duration variable problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi Victoria,

acc_SPTDuration [part4] is the sleep period time window. This is the time between sleep onset and wake.

dur_nightsleep_min [part5] is the portion of the sleep period time window that was labelled as sleep (or inactivity). You will notice that there are also 'dur_nightwak_ ..' variables in part5 output. The sum of dur_nightsleep_min and all of the dur_nightwak_ .. variables should equal the dur_night_min [part5] variable for that day. This is broken up in order to calculate sleep efficiency or to investigate the amount of movement over the night.

If you are only interested in the length of time between sleep onset and waking, then it would be best to use acc_SPTDuration from part4 output.

Good luck with it!

Matt

I've seen in the package manual that the latter is labelled as sleep duration but I have had some subjects with a value as low as 51 minutes (even though they went to bed at 19:07 and woke at 4:56). Why are the two variables sometimes so different and which one should I use for sleep duration?
>

>
> Victoria

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GENEActiv .csv epoch file
messages.body_plain:
GGIR is designed to process raw data files, sample rate of typically more than 20 Hertz.
GGIR does not handle aggregated data like the one you are trying to process. Please use the .bin file instead.

Vincent

I've attached the output from an example file. I'm not sure what else to try.

Many thanks,

Steph

messages.subject: problem comparing analyses with relyonsleeplog = TRUE/FALSE
messages.subject_clean: problem comparing analyses with relyonsleeplog = TRUE/FALSE
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have successfully analysed 14 nights of sleep for 6 participants in GGIR.

Participants have filled out a sleep diary and using relyonsleeplog = TRUE I get the following results for sleep duration:

id night_number dur_nightsleep_min_T0_yesdiary
15 2 385
15 3 469.75
15 4 421.4167
15 5 409.0833
15 6 392.1667
15 7 378.25
15 8 429.5
15 9 371.5
15 10 446.9167
15 11 367.6667
15 12 428.9167
15 13 399.4167

I would like to compare the GGIR analysis on the same data using relyonsleeplog = FALSE, to test if maybe we can ditch the sleep diary (which participants find cumbersome). For this analysis I get the following results:

id night_number dur_nightsleep_min_T0_nodiary
15 2 387
15 3 481.25
15 4 426.0833
15 5 411.4167
15 6 413.8333
15 7 388.5
15 8 440.75
15 9 381.3333
15 10 0
15 11
15 12
15 13
15 14

As you can see, the analysis using no sleep diary does not result in estimates beyound night #9. This is repeated in the results for the other 5 participants as well.

MY QUESTION IS: do I need to change other parameters, beyond  relyonsleeplog = TRUE=>FALSE, to make GGIR analyse more than 9 nights of sleep with no sleep log?

Best regards, Morten

P.S: Here is my GGIR script:

library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
             # INPUT NEEDED:
             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
             datadir=  "E:/Projekter/Axivity - Sleep/2. OmGui_Exported WAV-files/Gruppe 2019-04_t3",
             outputdir="E:/Projekter/Axivity - Sleep/6. GGIR_Output files",
             f0=1, f1=c(),
             idloc=2, # participant id number extracted from: 1=file header, 2=numbers before the underscore "_" in the filename
             snloc=2, # watch serial number extracted from: 1=file header, 2=numbers after the underscore "_" in the filename
             desiredtz="Europe/Copenhagen",
             overwrite=TRUE, #overwrites previously created milestone data
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
             do.enmo = TRUE,             do.anglez=TRUE,
             chunksize=1,                printsummary=TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 1,               ndayswindow=7,
             hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
             qwindow=c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
             mvpathreshold =c(100,120),
             bout.metric = 4,
             closedbout=FALSE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Sleep detection
             timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
             # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
             excludefirstlast = TRUE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(),
             loglocation= "E:/Projekter/Axivity - Sleep/4. Sleeplog_CSV-file/Gruppe 2019-04_t3/Gruppe 2019-04_t3.csv",
             outliers.only = TRUE,
             criterror = 4,
             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
             colid=1,
             coln1=2,
             do.visual = TRUE, #TRUE visualises only nights with a difference between sleeplog and sustained inactivity, FALSE visualises all nights
             nnights = 14,
             idloc=2, # id number drawn from: 1=file header, 2=numbers before the underscore in the filename
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             #-------------------------------
             threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
             boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1),   timewindow = c("WW"),
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data
             do.report=c(2,4,5),
             visualreport=TRUE,     dofirstpage = TRUE,
             viewingwindow=1)

On Mon, Jan 6, 2020 at 12:46 PM dominika <psd...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Vincent,
>
>
>
> Thank you for your comprehensive responses to my questions regarding ENMO metrics.
>
>
>
> In relation to the difference in nonwear time between day summary reports from parts 2 and 5, your response to the other post does not explain why the differences in the number of nonwear hours are striking for some subjects (please see the spreadsheet). For example, in part 2 day summary for subject #301 for day 4/9/2018, nonwear is reported as 24 hours. In part 5 day summary for the same subject and day, the number of valid hours is reported as 24 hours. I used MM. Empty spaces under part 5 indicate the lack of data for that day in part 5 relative to part 2. The discrepancies are highlighted.
>
>
>
> In part 2 of the code, I defined a valid day as at least 16 hours of wear.
>
>
>
> As there is no specific criterion provided for part 5, and vignette advises that the settings from part 2 are re-used in part 5 for calculation of sleep and physical activity data, I computed a criterion variable (Valid day), using a threshold of less than 33% of nonweartime (explicitly: “nonwear_perc_day” < 33) within a 24hr (midnight-to-midnight), which roughly corresponds to 16 hours criterion from part 5 (minus the decimal 0.3333. I would like to understand why in part 2 all hours would be considered valid while the opposite is the case in part 5 day summary report for some days?
>
>
>
> I attached the spreadsheet and my code for reference.
>
>
>
> Thank you in advance!
>
>
>
> Best,
>
>
>
> Dominika
>
>
>
> On Sunday, January 5, 2020 at 4:29:42 AM UTC-6, Vincent van Hees wrote:
> > See my other response from half an hour ago: Definitions of valid days between part 2 and part 5 can differ, because part 5 has criteria for both night (noon-noon) and daytime (midnight-midnight), while part2 only requires sufficient weartime during the day (midnight-midnight).

A related post by John “Difference in non-wear hours estimates between Part5 Day Summary and Person Summary output” reported on the differences between the valid number of hours between outputs from part 5 (day and person summaries).
> > >

> > > However, my concern pertains to the differences in the number of valid hours between parts 2 and 5-day summaries. I am using midnight to midnight window

messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent,

I realise that this is an old thread but I'm experiencing the same problem. Basically, I am getting the error messages described by the OP when trying to process GENEActiv bin files that we have previously processed (8 days of data collection), so we know the data should be there.

Steps I've taken: updated R, RStudio to latest versions, installed, updated, and loaded all of the dependent packages listed in the GGIR manual front page. Quit RStudio and restarted.  I get the same result using PC and Mac. Actigraph files process just fine so this is just a GENEActiv bin file issue.

Do you (or anyone) have any further updates on this issue?

cheers
Stuart

On Tuesday, 21 March 2017 15:20:30 UTC, Vincent van Hees wrote:

> Following on from my previous message. Just to clarify, the depencies on which GGIR relies are all R packages listed after 'Suggests', 'Imports', and 'Depends' on https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/index.html
>
> In R you can use the following command to install all of them in one go: install.packages("GGIR",dependencies = TRUE).
>
> At this moment this includes: MASS, signal, zoo, mmap, bitops, matlab, GENEAread,tuneR, testthat, covr, data.table, stats, utils
>
>

> On 21 March 2017 at 16:14, Vincent van Hees <vincent...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > Please find a below a summary of a correspondence I had with Pedro Pedro-Manuel...@chuv.ch and Mike yao...@nih.gov regarding an issue they encountered and the solution to address this issue:

> >
> > Original message by them: "We are trying to analyze the *.bin data from Geneactiv and we obtain the following error when importing the file
> >
> >
> >
> > [1] "File name: 5754__031468_2017-02-22 11-58-39.bin"
> >
> > Error in array(x, c(length(x), 1L), if (!is.null(names(x))) list(names(x),  :
> >
> >   'data' must be of a vector type, was 'NULL'
> >
> >
> >
> > The bin file was obtained directly from the Geneactiv device and is 715 Mb (15 days). We tried reading it using g.meta but it does not work. Do we also need to upload GENEAread?
> >
> >
> >
> > I attach the code. Do you have any idea why it is not working? We are running it on a Windows 7 professional environment, 24Gb RAM, and we run the code using Rstudio Version 0.99.879 and R version 3.2.3."
> >
> >
> > Final solution:
> >
> > Reinstall the R packages on which GGIR depends, because they are probably out of date. For example, mmap, bitops, matlab...
> >
> >
> > Vincent
